newsitem.title: USA: Clinton rating high, Congress low.
newsitem.headline: Clinton rating high, Congress low.

text.p: President Bill Clinton went into his State of the Union address on Tuesday with a job rating that was high while that of the Republican Congress was low, according to two new polls.

A CBS News Poll/New York Times poll between Jan. 30 and Feb. 1 said the Democratic president's job approval rating was 63 percent, highest in that poll since Clinton first took office. In the new poll his disapproval rating was 29 percent.
A poll between Jan. 14 and Jan. 17 gave him a 60 to 32 percent approval-disapproval rating.

A CNN/USA Today/Gallup poll also gave Clinton a high score -- a 60 percent favourable job rating against a 31 percent unfavourable rating for the period Jan. 30 to Feb. 2. A poll last month gave him a 62 percent favourable and 31 percent unfavourable job rating.
In the CNN/USA Today poll, Congress also got a low approval rating of 36 percent with 51 percent disapproving.
Both polls had a margin of error of plus or minus 3 percentage points in interviews of more than 1,000 people.

The approval rating of Congress in the CBS/Times poll has fallen to 36 percent from 45 percent approval before Clinton was inaugurated on Jan. 20. The number of those disapproving of the way Congress does its job meantime rose to 52 percent from 45 percent.

House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich, who has admitted to House Ethics Comittee charges he misled the House, which voted to remprimand him and assess a $300,000 penalty, has a very low 15 percent popularity rating in the CBS/Times pol. Fifty-five percent said they disliked him and the rest were undecided, offered no opinion or had not heard enough about him for an opinion.
However, the way Gingrich has been doing his job gets a higher rating in the CBS/Times poll, with 30 percent approving and 55 percent disapproving his job performance.

Not enough people -- 80 percent -- know Senate Republican leader Trent Lott, who took over that job from retired Sen. Bob Dole, to register a favourable or unfavourable opinion. Those who have heard of him gave him an 8 percent favourable rating against a 3 percent unfavourable job rating in the CBS/Times poll. Gingrich and Lott were not rated in the CNN/USA Today poll that was released on Tuesday.
